knowledge.retrieval.preset.qwen4.summary: Main workhorse for multilingual retrieval, long context, and shrinkable dimensions.
knowledge.retrieval.preset.qwen4.officia: The Qwen model card highlights instruction-aware retrieval, recommends English instructions for multilingual usage, and suggests flash_attention_2 for better memory efficiency.
knowledge.retrieval.preset.qwen4.setup: Prefer 12GB+ GPU memory or around 24GB of system RAM. For retrieval-only workloads, truncating to 1024 or 1536 dims cuts SQLite vector cost noticeably.
knowledge.retrieval.preset.qwen06.summar: Lightweight commercial-friendly option for multilingual retrieval and shrinkable dimensions.
knowledge.retrieval.preset.qwen06.offici: The Qwen model card gives the same instruction-aware guidance, recommends English instructions for multilingual use, and suggests flash_attention_2 for acceleration and memory savings.
knowledge.retrieval.preset.qwen06.setup: Prefer 4GB+ GPU memory or 8-12GB of system RAM. It is a stable choice for permissive commercial usage, local single-node runs, and light services.
Low-cost multilingual retrieval for CPU or single-GPU deployment.
The model card recommends xformers and unpadding. Its encoder-only design lowers hardware requirements and claims about a 10x inference speed gain over older decode-only GTE variants.
Prefer CPU or 3GB+ GPU memory. It fits multilingual retrieval services, lower-cost deployments, and Apache-2.0 requirements especially well.
knowledge.retrieval.preset.jinaSmall.sum: Retrieval-first with 32K context, suited for dedicated search services.
knowledge.retrieval.preset.jinaSmall.off: The model card recommends flash-attention and provides ONNX, vLLM, TEI, and GGUF deployment paths, so local and service deployments are both straightforward.
knowledge.retrieval.preset.jinaSmall.set: Prefer 6GB+ GPU memory or 8-12GB of system RAM. It is best for dedicated retrieval services, and truncating to 512 or 768 dims helps cut storage further.
knowledge.retrieval.preset.jinaNano.summ: Best for local experiments, laptops, and low-cost services.
knowledge.retrieval.preset.jinaNano.offi: The model card includes ONNX, vLLM, and GGUF usage. Flash-attention is recommended when available, but it is not required.
knowledge.retrieval.preset.jinaNano.setu: Prefer 2GB+ GPU memory or 4-6GB of system RAM. It is the best fit for laptops, local prototyping, and low-cost services.
knowledge.retrieval.preset.qwen8.summary: Quality-first option for multilingual complex retrieval and longer inputs.
knowledge.retrieval.preset.qwen8.officia: The model card emphasizes 100+ language coverage, instruction-aware retrieval, and fully shrinkable output dimensions. It is aimed squarely at quality-first workloads.
knowledge.retrieval.preset.qwen8.setup: Prefer 24GB+ GPU memory or 32GB+ of system RAM. Use it for quality-first multilingual and long-context retrieval where the higher cost is justified.
knowledge.retrieval.preset.bgeM3.summary: Upgrade path for hybrid retrieval with dense, sparse, and multi-vector outputs.
knowledge.retrieval.preset.bgeM3.officia: The model card explicitly recommends hybrid retrieval plus reranking, and notes that reducing max_length lowers latency directly.
knowledge.retrieval.preset.bgeM3.setup: Prefer 6GB+ GPU memory or 8-12GB of system RAM. Move to it when you are ready to invest in dense, sparse, and multi-vector retrieval together.

remoteAccess.enableWarning.title: Security warning
remoteAccess.enableWarning.message:
Remote access is experimental. Before turning it on, understand the risks:

• Paired devices can view sessions, files and knowledge in every project and send messages to agents. Agents read and write files and run commands on this computer under your current permission settings.
• Devices with full control can also approve tool calls and change files, git, knowledge and settings.
• Anyone holding a paired phone can operate this computer remotely. Revoke a device right away if it is lost or no longer used.
• Use it only on networks you trust. When exposing it through a tunnel or port forwarding, make sure the tunnel is encrypted and access is restricted.

Turn on remote access?

settings.item.system.debug.label: Debug Mode
settings.item.system.debug.desc: When enabled, runtime stalls, WebView connection health, and LLM HTTP requests are recorded. Dev builds use debug/llm/ and packaged builds use data/debug/llm/. Sensitive headers like Authorization are automatically redacted. It also stores the full request and response of every model call in the session database for context-export review, which uses significant disk space; takes effect from the next run.
settings.item.system.toolFailureLog.desc: Keep the latest 100 failed tool calls locally, including arguments, error output, and session location, for tool analysis and improvement. Disabled by default.
settings.item.system.closeBehavior.label: Close Behavior
settings.item.system.closeBehavior.desc: Choose what happens when the last window is closed.
settings.item.agent.sessionUndo.label: Session File Undo
settings.item.agent.sessionUndo.desc: Record each round of Agent file changes for session review and undo. Turning this off stops automatic Git snapshots and lets more writing tasks run concurrently.
settings.item.agent.tools.loadingMode.de: How lazily loaded tools are called: native (the provider's deferred loading), metaTool (through tool_call, keeping the tool list stable) or direct (as native tools on the next turn).
settings.item.agent.llm.retryMaxAttempts: How many times a failed model request is retried automatically (connection errors, timeouts, HTTP 5xx and 429 rate limits). Retries only happen before any output has streamed; 429 responses honor the server Retry-After header. Set 0 to disable.
settings.item.agent.llm.stripInlineThink: Route literal <think>/<thinking> prefixes from OpenAI-compatible endpoints into the thinking channel instead of the reply text.
settings.item.agent.subagent.maxDepth.de: Caps for the subagent tool. Max depth limits subagent nesting (1 = subagents cannot spawn subagents of their own); max concurrency limits how many subagents run at once per session. A subagent call past a cap returns an error to the agent naming the limit.
settings.item.agent.subagent.maxConcurre: Caps for the subagent tool. Max depth limits subagent nesting (1 = subagents cannot spawn subagents of their own); max concurrency limits how many subagents run at once per session. A subagent call past a cap returns an error to the agent naming the limit.
settings.item.permissions.fileWorkspaceB: Control whether file tools only run inside the workspace.
settings.item.providers.anthropic.native: Applies in Native dynamic tool loading mode. Turn off if a custom Base URL gateway rejects defer_loading / tool_reference, so requests skip the failed attempt and use the fallback directly.
settings.item.providers.claudeCode.enabl: Use Claude models through the claude command on this computer or an SSH server. Appears in the model list and API settings when enabled. Disabled by default.
settings.item.workspace.worktree.root.de: Base directory for new worktrees. Empty places them beside each repository; a launch option can override it for one run.
settings.item.workspace.resources.worksp: Idle time after which a checkout's watchers and lazily opened indexes are released.

settings.item.unity.enabled.desc: When off, Locus does not connect to the Unity Editor, scan assets, or offer Unity tools.
settings.item.unity.embed.enabled.label: Enable Unity embedded window
settings.item.unity.embed.enabled.desc: Show desktop content inside the Locus window in Unity. Turning this off stops creating and synchronizing embedded windows.
settings.item.unity.connection.nativeBri: Route Locus commands through the native broker loaded inside Unity so the connection survives domain reloads. Commands that need the native transport are unavailable while it is off; changes apply after the next domain reload.
settings.item.unity.connection.backgroun: Patches the Editor so it keeps serving Locus commands while unfocused or in the background, instead of stalling until you click back into Unity. Default on; native-symbol based, falls back automatically when unavailable.
settings.item.unity.connection.stateProb: Reads Unity's editor state from outside the process so status keeps updating during domain reloads and editor hangs, when the named pipe is silent. Falls back automatically when native symbols are unavailable.
settings.item.unity.externalEditor.autoS: Set Locus as Unity's default editor
When enabled, C# scripts open at their source line in the Locus asset preview. Locus remains available for manual selection in Unity External Tools.
settings.item.unity.codeAnalysis.csharpL: Semantic C# analysis backed by a Roslyn language server (downloaded on demand, loads the Unity-generated solution). All code_* tools require this to be on.
settings.item.unity.codeAnalysis.tools.c: Search C# symbols (classes, methods, fields) across the workspace.
Resolve a symbol to its declaration, including other assemblies and packages.
Semantically exact references to a symbol across the workspace.

Compiler and analyzer errors/warnings without compiling in Unity — the agent's verification loop after editing code. File scope also validates tag/layer/scene/Resources/Input string literals against the project settings.
settings.item.unity.codeAnalysis.tools.e: When the agent applies Unity C# changes, append semantic warnings for the current batch to the hot reload/recompile result. The standalone code_diagnostics tool can stay disabled.
settings.item.unity.codeAnalysis.tools.c: Exact signature, type and docs of a symbol (IDE hover) so the agent stops guessing APIs.
settings.item.unity.codeAnalysis.tools.u: Where a script or member is used inside scenes/prefabs/assets: attach points, UnityEvent bindings, serialized fields, AnimationEvents.
Inject Microsoft.Unity.Analyzers: Unity-specific diagnostics for code_diagnostics, plus suppression of misleading generic C# hints. Toggling restarts the analysis server.
settings.item.unity.compile.sidecar.desc: Compile unity_execute / unity_run_states snippets and View Scripts in a CoreCLR compile server (modern Roslyn) instead of inside the Unity Editor: faster compiles, no editor frame hitches in play mode, compile errors return without touching Unity. Any compile-server failure falls back to the in-Unity compiler automatically.
settings.item.unity.compile.inProcessFal: When the snippet compiler is on but unavailable, compile inside the Unity Editor instead of failing. Turn off to test the compile server in isolation.
settings.item.unity.compile.nonPublicAcc: Allow unity_execute and unity_run_states to directly access private and internal APIs and fields without reflection. The tool parameter can disable it for one call.
settings.item.unity.hotReload.enabled.de: Method-body C# edits become patch assemblies in the compile server and take effect in the running Editor within 1-2 seconds — no Unity recompile or domain reload. Signature/field changes still go through unity_recompile. Works in Release too: the few methods Mono inlines converge via an automatic recompile, and Debug avoids those recompiles.
settings.item.unity.hotReload.inlineForc: Evaluate inline risk with a stub
Let the Unity plugin force-JIT a synthetic caller stub to judge whether a hot-patched method is live yet, instead of relying only on a heuristic.
settings.item.unity.multiAgentEditor.des: Coordinate shared Unity Editor state such as Play Mode and recompilation with unity_lock and unity_release when multiple Agents use one Editor. Disabled by default.

settings.item.appearance.fonts.ui.desc: Font family for interface text. Empty uses the built-in font stack.
settings.item.appearance.fonts.prose.des: Font family for messages and documents. Empty uses the built-in font stack.
settings.item.appearance.fonts.monoInlin: Font family for inline code. Empty uses the built-in monospace stack.
settings.item.appearance.fonts.monoBlock: Font family for code blocks. Empty uses the built-in monospace stack.
settings.item.appearance.fonts.monoEdito: Font family for editors and terminals. Empty uses the built-in monospace stack.
settings.item.appearance.chrome.showWelc: Show the subtitle above the chat input of an empty session.
settings.item.appearance.chrome.showPlug: Show the Plugins tab in the top navigation.
settings.item.appearance.chrome.showAgen: Show the Agent tab in the top navigation.
settings.item.appearance.chrome.workspac: Show the title bar in workspace windows

Workspace windows other than the primary one also show the title bar with the Development, Plugins and Settings tabs. When off, those windows put the workspace toolbar in the title bar and open Plugins and Settings in separate windows.
settings.item.chat.messages.rightAlignUs: Align your own messages to the right of the session view.
settings.item.chat.messages.turnNavigati: Show the navigation rail for user turns when the session view has room for it.
settings.item.chat.messages.compactToolC: Collapse finished batches of tool calls in the session view.
settings.item.chat.messages.hideThinking: Hide the model's thinking once it has finished.
settings.item.chat.composer.showAgentSel: Show the Agent column in the model selector of the chat input.
settings.item.chat.history.pageSize.desc: Messages loaded when opening a session and each time you scroll up: 80, 120, 160, 240 or 400.
settings.item.chat.input.submitMode.desc: enter-send: Enter sends and Ctrl/Cmd+Enter inserts a newline. mod-enter-send: Ctrl/Cmd+Enter sends and Enter inserts a newline.
settings.item.chat.input.runningSendMode: What a message sent during an active run does: insert submits it into the current run; after-run queues it until the run finishes.
settings.item.shortcuts.newChat.label: New session shortcut
settings.item.shortcuts.newChat.desc: Key combination that starts a new session, e.g. ctrl+n. Empty uses the default (Ctrl+N, Cmd+N on macOS). Must include a modifier.
settings.item.shortcuts.cancelRun.label: Stop response shortcut
settings.item.shortcuts.cancelRun.desc: Key pressed twice to stop the active response, e.g. escape. Empty uses Esc. A single key is allowed.
settings.item.shortcuts.findInContext.de: Key combination that searches the focused document or list, e.g. ctrl+f. Empty uses the default (Ctrl+F, Cmd+F on macOS).
settings.item.shortcuts.globalSearch.des: Key combination that opens global search, e.g. ctrl+shift+f. Empty uses the default (Ctrl+Shift+F, Cmd+Shift+F on macOS).
settings.item.workbench.tabs.mountedSess: Loaded session tabs per editor group
Hidden session tabs kept loaded in each workbench editor group: 1, 2, 3, 6 or 10; 0 keeps all of them loaded. Tabs beyond the limit unload to save memory and reload when shown.
settings.item.workbench.panels.todoAutoO: Open the TODO panel when the agent writes todos.
settings.item.workbench.panels.changesAu: Open the file changes panel when files change.
Close the file changes panel when you send a new message.
settings.item.workbench.panels.fileChang: Show a preview when hovering a changed file.
settings.item.workbench.open.chatDiffRev: Where session file changes open for review: inline (current window) or window (separate window).
settings.item.workbench.open.gitDiffRevi: Where Git file changes open for review: inline (current window) or window (separate window).
settings.item.workbench.open.planApprova: Where a plan waiting for approval is shown: card (in the session) or window (separate window).
Where Memory document references open: knowledge (Knowledge page) or window (separate Markdown preview).
settings.item.workbench.open.view.label: Open Views in
settings.item.workbench.open.view.desc: Default target when opening a View: tab or window.
settings.item.workbench.open.viewOverrid: Open target overrides for individual Views (tab or window), keyed by workspace and View id. Views without an entry use workbench.open.view.
settings.item.workbench.open.assetRefCli: What clicking a Unity asset reference in a session does: locusInspector (Workbench tab), unityInspector (Unity's Inspector), unitySelect (select in Unity only) or fileBrowser (reveal the file).
settings.item.workbench.open.unityEmbedA: Asset reference click action in Unity embed
Click action for asset references in the window embedded in the Unity Editor; same values as workbench.open.assetRefClick.
settings.item.workbench.views.showInSess: List View packages in the lower part of the session list.
settings.item.workbench.git.mergeTreeSta: Show Git status in the file tree as colored file icons instead of status letters.
settings.item.workbench.git.hideCommandS: Hide command suggestions in the Git terminal.
settings.item.documents.punctuationPairi: Automatically close Chinese and English quotes and brackets in documents, chat and other text fields.
settings.item.documents.commentAuthor.de: Name shown on your document comments (up to 64 characters).
settings.item.notifications.system.enabl: Send desktop notifications for key chat events while Locus is not focused.
settings.item.notifications.system.onCha: Send a notification when a chat run completes.
settings.item.notifications.system.onSub: Send a notification when a subagent run completes.
settings.item.notifications.system.onAsk: Send a notification when the agent asks you a question.
settings.item.notifications.system.onCha: Send a notification when a chat run fails.
settings.item.notifications.system.onToo: Send a notification when a tool call waits for your approval.
settings.item.notifications.sound.enable: Play a sound for key chat events.
settings.item.notifications.sound.mode.d: Built-in sound style: soft, bright or urgent.
settings.item.notifications.sound.source: builtin plays the built-in sounds; custom plays notifications.sound.customFile.
settings.item.notifications.sound.custom: Audio file played when the sound source is custom.
settings.item.notifications.sound.onChat: Play a sound when a chat completes
Play a sound when a chat run completes.
settings.item.notifications.sound.onSuba: Play a sound when a subagent completes
Play a sound when a subagent run completes.
settings.item.notifications.sound.onAskU: Play a sound when input is needed
Play a sound when the agent asks you a question.
settings.item.notifications.sound.onChat: Play a sound when a chat fails
Play a sound when a chat run fails.
settings.item.notifications.sound.onTool: Play a sound when approval is needed
Play a sound when a tool call waits for your approval.
settings.item.notifications.hints.cacheI: Show an in-app warning when a request that should have reused the prompt cache missed it.
settings.project.title: Current project: {0}
settings.project.desc: Stored in this project's Locus/config.json. Applies to this project only and can be shared with the repository.
settings.project.none: No project is focused in this window. Open a workspace to change its project settings here.
settings.project.knowledgeEnabledDesc: When off, this project does not use knowledge documents, knowledge tools or knowledge injection, and the workspace tree hides its knowledge section.
settings.project.markdownImages.unset: Not set — asked on the first paste
settings.project.markdownImages.incomple: Fill in both the document folder and the image folder.
settings.unity.diagnosticsDesc: Live state of the focused workspace's Unity editor and services, with self-tests. The switches above apply to every workspace.
settings.unity.diagnosticsNone: No workspace is focused in this window. Open a Unity workspace to see the live state and self-tests of code analysis, compilation and the connection here.
settings.unity.testPackageReady: Version {0} installed; tests can be discovered and run
settings.unity.selfTestDesc: Runs real checks against the current project: editor connection, compilation, code execution, hot reload and more. The run options decide whether the plugin is installed, Unity is launched and Play Mode is exited automatically.
settings.item.latex.engine.label: Engine
settings.item.latex.engine.desc: A % !TEX program comment at the top of the file wins. Auto: LuaLaTeX for LuaTeX-only packages, pdfLaTeX for classic documents that load inputenc, XeLaTeX otherwise.
settings.item.latex.preview.svg.label: SVG preview
settings.item.latex.preview.svg.desc: When off, only the PDF is shown. The SVG preview injects the dvisvgm driver at compile time without editing the source; a PDF is always compiled as cache and fallback.
settings.item.latex.toolchain.allowPacka: When off, builds pass --disable-installer and a missing package fails the build. MiKTeX helpers such as font generation ignore this option and follow MiKTeX's own setting.
settings.latex.toolchainDesc: Detected from PATH and the default MiKTeX and TeX Live install folders.
settings.latex.dvisvgmMissing: dvisvgm was not found; previews can only show the PDF.
latexPreview.status.pending: Changed; updates while the preview is visible
latexPreview.status.errorKeepsLast: Build failed; showing the last successful result
latexPreview.fallback.sticky: The SVG preview failed for this document before, so the PDF is shown; Rebuild retries SVG
latexPreview.empty.failed: The build failed and there is no result to show.
